headline: KSE-100 holds flat at 174,929.68 as a hot CPI print and a stingy T-bill auction keep the SBP boxed in — refineries, E&P and cash-rich banks stay the desk's picks into the Sept 14 MPC.
summary: KSE-100 closed basically flat today (174,929.68, +0.09%) after two rough sessions — a pause, not a turnaround. The macro backdrop stays risk-off: August CPI came in hot at 11.1% YoY, SBP looks locked into an extended hold into its Sept 14 meeting, and today's T-bill auction saw the government raise less than it wanted (Rs680bn vs an Rs800bn target) while yields on the belly of the curve crept higher. Globally, Brent crude keeps climbing (+15% this month) and gold just jumped nearly 4% in a day — a safe-haven signal that undercuts the calmer VIX. The desk stays selective: refineries and large, well-funded banks over broad-market exposure.

sectors.name: Refineries
sectors.why: Brent at $96.40/bbl (+15% this month per global.json) keeps refining margins wide, and both ATRL and NRL are showing live technical strength — NRL even carries a proven-strategy breakout trigger.

sectors.name: Banks (large-cap)
sectors.why: Today's T-bill auction saw yields on the belly of the curve rise even as the short end eased — a carry tailwind for big banks sitting on government paper; small, thinly-capitalized banks don't get the same benefit.

sectors.name: Oil & Gas E&P
sectors.why: POL and OGDC ride the same Brent rally as the refiners with cheap-to-fair valuations and firm technicals, but macro.json's own sector tilt doesn't name E&P as favoured — it's a crude-price bet, not a structural pick.

sectors.name: OMCs
sectors.why: Squeezed between a near-daily-reset pump price and the rising import cost of the fuel itself as Brent keeps climbing — explicitly on the desk's avoid list.

sectors.name: Autos, cement & power/IPPs
sectors.why: Rate-sensitive and import-cost exposed, with power/IPPs also carrying the unresolved circular-debt overhang ahead of the IMF's September review.

watchlist.angle: Refinery play with a live signal: dashboard.json shows a medium-confidence donchian55_break trigger (55.5% historical hit rate, +2.08% average net edge over 60 backtested trades) — sits inside the desk's favoured refinery sector as Brent pushes to $96.40/bbl. Fundamentals are cheap on P/E (7.13, cheapest third of PSX) but thin on margin (1.4%) and pay no dividend, so this reads as a momentum/sector-tailwind case, not a value one.
watchlist.risk: No dividend cushion and a thin margin mean the stock has little to fall back on if the technical breakout fails or crude reverses.

watchlist.angle: Refinery name stacking three things at once: RSI 63.2 and price above both moving averages (up 18.4% over the last 20 sessions per quant.json), a cheap-and-improving fundamentals card (P/E 4.9, forward P/E 3.45), and a confirmed Rs15/share dividend going ex on 2026-10-12.
watchlist.risk: Already run hard (+18% in a month) — a lot of the refining-margin optimism may be priced in, and net margin is still thin at 7.6%.

watchlist.angle: Attractive-rated bank (P/E 6.26, forward P/E 4.49, 17.1% net margin, an 8.58% dividend yield covered at a 54% payout) with a dated near-term catalyst: shares go ex-dividend 2026-09-10 (book closure 09-11, Rs1.6/share). Fits the desk's favoured large-bank theme as the T-bill curve's belly firms.
watchlist.risk: Beta 1.2 means it moves more than the market — in a risk-off tape that cuts both ways.

watchlist.angle: Cheapest-on-paper E&P name on the board: P/E 6.17 (cheapest third of PSX), a 53% net margin, and a confirmed Rs72.5/share dividend (9.94% yield) going ex 2026-10-12. Technicals are constructive too — RSI 63.9, above both moving averages, +6.33% over 20 sessions — riding the same Brent rally driving the desk's energy tilt.
watchlist.risk: Forward P/E (7.4) is actually higher than trailing (6.17) — the market isn't pricing further earnings growth here, so this is a mature story, not a re-rating one; a crude pullback removes the tailwind fast.

watchlist.angle: Large-cap E&P with a mixed-but-improving fundamentals card (P/E 9.09, forward 7.32, 39.8% net margin, a 4.71% covered dividend) and firming technicals (RSI 53.9, above both moving averages). Results are expected around 2026-09-04 per the earnings calendar — a near-term catalyst worth watching, though the exact date isn't fully confirmed.
watchlist.risk: Sits outside the desk's explicitly favoured sector list (only refineries and large banks are named) — this is a macro-oil bet more than a value pick, and its own forward multiple already assumes higher profits.

catalysts.event: OGDC, PSO and SHFA results expected (date unconfirmed) — first read on the oil majors since the Brent rally accelerated
SBP Monetary Policy Committee decision — an extended hawkish hold is the base case after the confirmed 11.1% CPI print
POL, ATRL, APL and HUBC all go ex-dividend the same day — POL Rs72.5/share (9.94% yield), ATRL Rs15/share

risks: Brent crude is up 15% in a month and the desk's geo-risk composite rose to 63/100 — a big chunk of today's favoured refinery/E&P thesis rests on oil staying elevated; a ceasefire or supply resolution would hit ATRL, NRL, POL and OGDC together.

August CPI printed 11.1% YoY and today's T-bill auction fell short of its raise target (Rs680bn vs Rs800bn) even as yields on the belly of the curve rose — a sign the state is paying up for funding, which pressures broader equity valuations and locks the SBP into an extended hold.

Data-coverage caveat: state/health.json flags 262 of 455 tracked symbols with no fresh bar since 2026-08-22 (a refresh-rotation gap); every name on tonight's watchlist checked fresh as of 2026-09-03, but it's a live gap in the desk's broader data breadth.
